questions.q: What is the single most common cause of a company ending up multi-platform, per this lesson?
options: Mergers and acquisitions, which hand the acquiring company whatever platform the acquired company ran
A DBA team randomly deciding to install a second database engine
Database vendors requiring companies to use multiple platforms
Government regulation mandating platform diversity
questions.explain: When Company A acquires Company B, Company A inherits Company B's production database estate on whatever platform it already runs.

questions.q: Why does a legacy application often stay on its original database platform for years, even after a company standardizes on something else?
options: The application may be too deeply customized or too critical to rewrite, and it still does its job
It is technically impossible to run legacy applications on newer platforms
Legacy applications always run faster than modern ones
Companies are legally required to keep old systems unchanged
questions.explain: Replacing a working, deeply customized legacy system is a high-risk, expensive project that often never gets prioritized.

questions.q: Which is a real, deliberate reason a team might choose PostgreSQL for a new project, per this lesson?
options: Extensibility such as JSON support and extensions like PostGIS, plus avoiding licensing costs on non-core infrastructure
PostgreSQL is required by law for new software projects
PostgreSQL is the only platform capable of storing relational data
PostgreSQL automatically converts data from other platforms
questions.explain: Teams often choose PostgreSQL deliberately for its extensibility and open-source licensing model, not because other platforms can't do the job.

questions.q: How does licensing cost pressure typically play out as a migration, per this lesson?
options: Gradually, system by system over years, meaning old and new platforms run side by side for a long time
As a single clean cutover completed in a weekend
It never actually results in any migration
By deleting the old system's data immediately
questions.explain: Cost-driven migrations off Oracle or SQL Server toward open-source platforms happen incrementally, not all at once.

questions.q: According to this lesson, why does full platform standardization rarely happen in practice?
options: Migrations are expensive and risky, some legacy systems are poorly understood, some vendor apps require a specific platform, and the business case is often weak
It is technically impossible for two database platforms to coexist in one company
Standardization is illegal under most software licensing agreements
Every company successfully standardizes on one platform eventually
questions.explain: The lesson lists concrete practical barriers that make full standardization rare, framing multi-platform environments as the normal, expected state.
